thread:
ryan: Heads-up: noticed conflicting examples for handling sequence limits across the model catalog and SDK docs. One example shows client-side truncation, another shows server-side error. We should standardize, add a short migration note for SDK v4, and update benchmark notes for long-context models. Who can own a small PR?

mira: I can take this. plan: 1) pick canonical behavior (client truncation with explicit warning), 2) update model catalog notes to reference SDK change, 3) add an SDK snippet showing pre-tokenization + streaming fallback. ETA tomorrow.

toni: +1 on client-side truncation. We saw better UX that way and fewer 4xx spikes in traffic. Also add a note about tokenization differences between tokenizers (bpe vs unigram) and a sample check to verify length pre-send.

sam: I'll contribute a micro-benchmark for M-long-context variants showing latency and memory at 2k/8k/32k seqs. Put the table in docs/examples/longseq-bench.html. Also will include the exact commands used to run the bench infra.

mira: Draft PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/912 — includes standardized guidance, three SDK snippets (sync truncation, async streaming fallback, and pre-tokenizer check), bench results, and a short migrations.md with recommended change logs.

toni: Quick nit: can we avoid the word "fail-open" in the snippet names, use "stream-fallback" instead? It reads clearer.

mira: Good call — renamed. Pushed changes.

sam: Bench results summary: for orion-8k model variant we saw mean latency (per-request) 92ms @2k, 350ms @8k, 1.4s @32k with batching disabled; RAM tripled at 32k. I added those numbers and the test harness commands.

ryan: For SDK v4 example, include both a small JS snippet and Python snippet. JS should show how to call streaming fallback when the client detects > max_tokens. Also call out tokenization lib & version.

mira: Added two snippets. JS:
```javascript
// check and truncate before send
const tokens = tokenizer.encode(prompt);
if (tokens.length > model.max_tokens) {
  const truncated = tokenizer.decode(tokens.slice(-model.max_tokens));
  // send truncated prompt and set metadata.warn_truncated = true
}
```
Python streaming fallback snippet:
```python
# if payload exceeds limit, stream chunks
for chunk in chunked_inputs(inputs, model.max_tokens):
    resp = client.generate(chunk, stream=True)
    for token in resp:
        process(token)
```

toni: Also add an explicit compatibility note in the model metadata: "server truncation is deprecated for public APIs; private deployments may opt-in". Teams with private infra should be told to contact infra for a grace period.

mira: Added that to the model metadata section and linked to the private-deploy guide.

docbot: CI started for PR #912 — running docs-lint, linkcheck, and preview build.

docbot: CI found two broken links in migration.md: tokenizers/version-history and infra/streaming-fallback.

mira: Fixing links now. Also added a tiny acceptance test that smoke-runs the JS snippet via node: node examples/snippets/truncate-check.js

sam: Re-ran bench with batching enabled; numbers look different. I added a short paragraph explaining how batching config changes tail latency in longseq workloads and linked to the batching guide.

ryan: One editorial: can we add a one-paragraph "what changed" at the top of migration.md so eng teams immediately know if they need to change code? Also include a single diff snippet showing before/after in Python.

mira: Done. Top-of-page TL;DR added and python diff included.

docbot: CI passed for PR #912. Preview: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr-912/sequence-limits-standardization.html

toni: Quick visual review on preview — looks good. Left one tiny wording suggestion about "edge case" behavior when using model-variants with shorter kv_cache.

mira: Addressed wording. Planning to merge after one more LGTM.

sam: LGTM. :white_check_mark:

mira: Merged PR #912 -> main.

docbot: Publish event: docs update published to production, path: /guides/sequence-limits-standardization.html, timestamp 3481234599

ryan: Thanks! After publish, let's ping product and dev-ex so SDK users notice the migration note. I'll draft the release blurb.

mira: Thanks all. Follow-up: open a small follow-up issue to track adding an automated lint that checks examples for outdated truncation examples.

toni: Filed issue #1742 for example-lint.

sam: added a short note in the model-catalog change log about the bench variance at 32k and the recommended batching knobs.

ryan: Perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround.
